description:
Make a git-mode snapshot export read every captured file through one git module object reader, instead of opening libgit2 once per file.

## Background

- In git mode, capture reads each file through `read_content` (`crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs:196-204`), which opens a libgit2 repository per file and calls `read_from_git` (`crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs:138-172`). That function returns the blob bytes with the commit and the blob id as `blob_sha`, and fails with `NotFoundError` "Path '<path>' not found in commit <ref>" (exit 3).
- Asset paths come from scanning documents read in the same export, so reads arrive after earlier answers.
- Tests: `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/snapshot_export_tests.rs`.
- Kept as one change for a build reason: `read_from_git` is private, and an uncalled private method fails the zero-warning build.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A git-mode export reads every file it captures through one object reader on the executor's git checkout, recording each file's blob id as `blob_sha` and the commit as today. `read_from_git` and the per-file repository open no longer exist, and `commands/snapshot.rs` uses no git2.
- [hard] REQ-02: A missing path fails with today's not-found error and exit 3, working-tree exports are unchanged, and the snapshot export tests pass.
- [hard] REQ-03: A CLI test with the counting stand-in first on `PATH` exports `--at HEAD` over several documents and assets and asserts one `cat-file` invocation; today export runs in libgit2 and records none, so it fails.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Snapshot export reads committed files through one git process
